facts.raw_span: An 82-year-old man with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma (cT1N0M0)
was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab
new bilateral infiltrative shadows
He reported fever and dyspnea
elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative

Serologic testing for anti–nuclear antigen, anti–aminoacyl–tRNA synthetase, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide, anti-Sjögren’s-syndrome-related antigen A and B, and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antigen antibodies were all negative
no history of antigen exposure
grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis was suspected
bronchoscopy showed no airway secretions
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages, and a CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.33

concepts.why: The patient developed bilateral infiltrative shadows and symptoms consistent with pneumonitis after receiving ipilimumab and nivolumab, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed a high percentage of lymphocytes.
The patient did not respond to methylprednisolone treatment, indicating a refractory form of ICI-induced pneumonitis.
The patient was diagnosed with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma, a type of cancer that affects the lining of the lungs.
The patient developed ICI-induced pneumonitis, which is a result of immune system dysregulation caused by the treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab.
The patient presented with fever and dyspnea, and laboratory tests showed elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels, indicating an inflammatory response.
The patient developed bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT, which is consistent with pulmonary infiltrates.
The bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed a high percentage of lymphocytes, indicating lymphocytic inflammation.
The bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed a significant percentage of neutrophils, indicating neutrophilic inflammation.
The patient did not respond to methylprednisolone treatment, indicating corticosteroid resistance.
It explains the negative sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR, as well as the negative serologic testing for various autoantibodies, in the context of pneumonitis.

rationales.F01: Patient's age and diagnosis of epithelioid pleural mesothelioma are neutral for most concepts, but strongly suggest C03.
rationales.F02: Treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab increases the likelihood of ICI-induced pneumonitis and immune system dysregulation.
rationales.F03: New bilateral infiltrative shadows are a key feature of pulmonary infiltrates and suggest ICI-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F05: Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels indicate an inflammatory response and are consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F07: Negative sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR help rule out other causes of pneumonitis.
rationales.F08: Negative serologic testing for various antibodies reduces the likelihood of autoimmune pneumonitis.
rationales.F10: The clinical picture and imaging are consistent with grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F12: The results of the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis are consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis and lymphocytic inflammation.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's clinical picture, including new bilateral infiltrative shadows after ipilimumab and nivolumab treatment, and lack of improvement with steroid treatment, supports the diagnosis of steroid-refractory ICI-induced pneumonitis.
